query: Starting from a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix, what single intervention could overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention, the proposed mechanism, the predicted comparative outcome, the applicable processing and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of high-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering will improve the thermal conductivity of the W-Cu composite by 20% compared to the untreated composite, due to the formation of a homogeneous distribution of W and Cu phases with enhanced interfacial contact and reduced voids.
generation.material_initial_state: W-Cu composite with W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix
generation.intervention: High-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering
generation.conditions: Ball milling at 200 rpm for 5 hours, SPS at 800°C for 30 minutes under 50 MPa
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a homogeneous distribution of W and Cu phases with enhanced interfacial contact and reduced voids
generation.mechanism: Mechanical alloying during ball milling breaks down W and Cu phases, creating fresh surfaces that facilitate interdiffusion and bonding during SPS, thereby reducing phase separation and interfacial voids
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved thermal conductivity by 20% compared to the untreated composite
generation.boundary: Heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in thermal conductivity may vary depending on the specific ball milling and SPS conditions, as well as the stability of the W-Cu composite under irradiation conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the thermal conductivity of the W-Cu composite after high-energy ball milling and SPS to that of the untreated composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermal conductivity of the treated composite is not significantly improved compared to the untreated composite, the hypothesis is falsified

proposals.material_system: W–Cu composite with W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix
proposals.intervention: High-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) with an optimized holding time and temperature
proposals.conditions: Ball milling at 200 rpm for 5 hours, SPS at 800°C for 30 minutes under 50 MPa
proposals.structural_mediator: Formation of a homogeneous distribution of W and Cu phases with enhanced interfacial contact and reduced voids
proposals.mechanism: Mechanical alloying during ball milling breaks down W and Cu phases, creating fresh surfaces that facilitate interdiffusion and bonding during SPS, thereby reducing phase separation and interfacial voids
proposals.predicted_outcome: Improved thermal conductivity by 20% compared to the untreated composite, due to enhanced interfacial contact and reduced scattering of phonons and electrons at interfaces
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: The intervention targets the root causes of phase separation and interfacial void formation, which are critical for improving thermal conductivity under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions

proposals.material_system: W–Cu composite with W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix
proposals.intervention: Introduction of a Ti interlayer between W and Cu phases during composite fabrication
proposals.conditions: Ti interlayer thickness of 100 nm, deposited by magnetron sputtering
proposals.structural_mediator: Formation of a Ti-rich interlayer that enhances interfacial bonding and reduces void formation
proposals.mechanism: The Ti interlayer acts as a wetting agent, improving the interfacial contact between W and Cu phases, and reducing the energy barrier for interdiffusion and bonding
proposals.predicted_outcome: Improved thermal conductivity by 15% compared to the untreated composite, due to enhanced interfacial contact and reduced scattering of phonons and electrons at interfaces
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: The intervention targets the interfacial properties that are critical for improving thermal conductivity under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions

proposals.material_system: W–Cu composite with W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix
proposals.intervention: Irradiation with high-energy ions (e.g., He+) to create defects and enhance interfacial mixing
proposals.conditions: Irradiation at 500°C with 100 keV He+ ions to a fluence of 1 × 10^17 ions/cm^2
proposals.structural_mediator: Creation of defects and enhanced interfacial mixing, leading to improved interfacial contact and reduced voids
proposals.mechanism: The irradiation-induced defects enhance interdiffusion and bonding between W and Cu phases, reducing phase separation and interfacial voids
proposals.predicted_outcome: Improved thermal conductivity by 10% compared to the untreated composite, due to enhanced interfacial contact and reduced scattering of phonons and electrons at interfaces
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: The intervention targets the interfacial properties that are critical for improving thermal conductivity under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions

proposals.material_system: W–Cu composite with W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix
proposals.intervention: Addition of a small amount of a third element (e.g., Ni) to the Cu matrix to enhance interfacial bonding and reduce void formation
proposals.conditions: Addition of 2 at.% Ni to the Cu matrix, followed by annealing at 600°C for 2 hours
proposals.structural_mediator: Formation of a Ni-rich interlayer that enhances interfacial bonding and reduces void formation
proposals.mechanism: The Ni addition enhances the interfacial contact between W and Cu phases, reducing the energy barrier for interdiffusion and bonding
proposals.predicted_outcome: Improved thermal conductivity by 12% compared to the untreated composite, due to enhanced interfacial contact and reduced scattering of phonons and electrons at interfaces
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: The intervention targets the interfacial properties that are critical for improving thermal conductivity under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions
